scope: Quick Checklist at 10 and 1,000 rows, one shown window. Debug Swift test harness (BenchmarkTests.themeDragCost), system WKWebView on macOS 26.6.2, Apple M1. Single run per row count.
question: Does a color drag in the theme panel need its own preview path or a frame-rate cap, now that a theme change is an owner edit saved by the save jobs?

method.drag: 120 DocumentSession.changeTheme(.set) calls 16 ms apart (a 60 Hz picker), then flush
method.change_to_style_ms: From each change (Swift wall clock) to the page's MutationObserver seeing --slop-accent set (performance.timeOrigin + now). A delivery that skips superseded changes counts from the earliest change it covers. The two clocks differ by under a millisecond, so values near zero can be slightly negative.
method.frames: requestAnimationFrame does not run for the harness window, so frame times were not recorded

finding: Accepting a change in memory and delivering the latest palette keeps a drag live without a page-only preview: at 1,000 rows delivery trails by about one frame and skips superseded colors, and the final color always shows. No frame-rate cap is needed. Saves are not per change: autosave and flush write the palette with the document.
